decision: convert orchestrator plans into durable capability-gated mission chains
scope: lab orchestration and synthetic workers only
winner: thin OrchestratedMissionRuntime adapter over existing planner and MissionCoordinator

comparison.approach: thin adapter over planner + durable coordinator
comparison.correctness: high: planner output becomes persisted dependency-ordered missions with per-agent capability gates
comparison.robustness: high for coordinator restart and submission retry through derived idempotency keys
comparison.latency: moderate: one durable snapshot per planned agent mission
comparison.regressionRisk: low: existing planner and queue semantics remain separate
comparison.qa: restart persistence, submission idempotency, capability and dependency ordering

comparison.approach: rewrite orchestrator to own persistence and worker state
comparison.robustness: medium until duplicated queue semantics are proven
comparison.regressionRisk: high due to duplicated scheduling/state-machine behavior
comparison.qa: would require replacing broad existing coverage

comparison.approach: direct dispatch from planner without durable missions
comparison.regressionRisk: medium operational risk from lost work

whyItWon: It closes the actual planner-to-durable-queue integration gap without merging routing, persistence, and worker execution into one component. It preserves low regression surface while making every selected agent explicit, durable, capability-gated work.
lessons: Serial dependency chaining is conservative and deterministic but sacrifices parallelism among independent agents; fan-out plus review joins should be evaluated next.
Derived per-agent idempotency keys make submission retry stable only when planner membership is stable for the same logical submission.
This is not evidence for multiple live coordinators sharing one snapshot file.
Real Qubes remains blocked until full QA is green and process/VM-boundary fault tests pass.
